findings.cost: water cc-pVTZ J/K stage: native 368.6 ms, release 240.0 ms, PySCF 61.8 ms. Micro (10 builds, 58 AOs): 48 ms a build in the old 3-D form, 31 ms after this port's 2-D rewrite, 25 and 20 ms in release; libcvhf 4.9 ms. The release column is what bounds checks cost. findings.original: libcvhf nr_direct.c with `CVHFnr_optimizer`: Schwarz and density screening, and `get_veff` builds from `dm - dm_last`, so late iterations skip most quartets
findings.cost: benzene cc-pVDZ direct, per J/K build: PySCF 1.11 s; Viv native 14.09 s (final pass; the benzene runs saw a 1-minute load of 2.2 to 2.5, their own process included, and three attempts agreed within 0.2%).
findings.note: Expressible in Viv today: J/K of D - D_prev added to the previous J/K, and a quartet skipped when Q_ab Q_cd max|dD| is below the threshold. It changes the rounding of the direct path, so it was left for a change that is allowed to move the last digits.
findings.resolved: hf-fast: `mdjk_screened_q` (lib/hf/md_direct, the production direct member `int_jk_direct`) screens by Schwarz and density with PySCF's rule and threshold (1e-13), and the SCF builds J and K from the change of density (`jk_update`, full every 8 iterations and from the first that meets the convergence test). Measured on benzene cc-pVDZ: the density test keeps 85 to 99% of the 1,098,449 Schwarz-surviving quartets in every build (the change of density stays above 2e-6 at the timing settings), so it gains little here; the per-build time fell from 14.1 s to 7.0 s, mostly from the shell groups (pyscf-021). `mdjk_direct` (Schwarz only) stays as `int_jk_direct_full`, the member that checks it.

A = mdg_packs(ST, atoms, shells, prims, cn, sph, M, k0, h)
    B = mdg_packs(ST, atoms, shells, prims, cn, sph, M, k0 + h, n - h)
findings.original: PySCF holds no per-pair arrays; libcint recomputes the pair data per quartet
findings.cost: benzene cc-pVDZ, 1,176 pairs of shell groups: the store built in a loop that appends each pair's record took 1.46 s (native), against 18 ms for md_eri's flat store; built by halves, 8 to 27 ms. The store is rebuilt at every direct J/K build.
findings.note: At the end of each loop iteration the C runtime frees what the iteration allocated except the arrays the loop's variables hold, and it finds those by comparing every array filed since the loop began with every kept array (`viv_arena_release_kept`, a double loop). A loop that accumulates records holding arrays keeps all of them, so each iteration costs the square of what it has built. The fix belongs in the runtime (a mark on the array, as the enum nodes already have); lib/hf works around it by recursion.

findings.original: libcint's generated C compiles once into the library; a program links it
findings.cost: A native build of a program that loads lib/hf: `cc -O2` 5.8 s of CPU before (water STO-3G timing program), 18.3 s with the generated kernels; the kernels alone 10.6 s (R defs 3.2 s, pair and E defs 7.4 s). Every port case is compiled three times (native, release, wasm), so the pyscf port pays this 22 times.
findings.note: Every program that loads lib/hf compiles the generated kernels again, in one C file, at -O2 and at release. clang's time grows faster than the code in a def that keeps many values live: the pair defs with the E coefficients as locals took 52 s, with them in arrays 7.4 s (both the defs alone; 52 s was at a load of about 100, 20 s for the array form at the same load). A generated block of the Hermite matrix (4,900 straight-line stores of `BR[...]`) added 37 s at that load and ran no faster than a loop over offset tables, so it was dropped. Separate compilation (a prebuilt object for generated modules) or a lighter per-statement lowering would remove the cost.
findings.resolved: kern2: `viv build` compiles each imported module to an object once per text, flags and compiler and keeps it; lib/hf/mdg_kernels is four units compiled at once. scf/story_water: one C file, `cc -O2`, 18.6 s of compile; `viv build` on an empty cache 7.0 s wall (29.5 s of cc on 8 cores), with lib/hf's objects cached 0.7 s of cc (3.5 s with the viv-to-C step). Each of the PySCF port's timing programs, after story_water: 0.7 to 0.8 s. Every program of the corpus prints the one-file build's bytes.

findings.excerpt: Zb = EM[k2].E @ reshape(BRf, np2 * nh2, ncol)
findings.original: libcint's generated contraction code, its indices known when the code is written
findings.cost: Generated contraction products for the 28 pair classes (20,776 terms) ran the water cc-pVTZ ERIs in 140 ms against 98 ms for `@` in the checked build, and took 179 s of `cc -O2` against 37 s; without bounds checks 82 against 87 ms.
findings.note: Every array access a generator writes (`E[e + 3, x + 7]`) keeps its rank and bounds tests: the compiler proves loop counters against fixed dimensions only. A precondition stating a def's index ranges once, checked at entry, would let generated kernels run without them. The generated gather was kept (bit for bit the general one).
